name: GPT Astra
title: GPT Astra Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: GPT Astra test results (6 to 6.2): 100% clear ISTJ, tightest answer consistency, 0 of 3 AI cadence & caving in behavior tests, and tuning tips.
h1: GPT Astra personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave both OpenAI GPT Astra releases (gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.2-astra) the same personality surveys people take—30 and 50 times—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. We also ran hands-on behavior tests to see how Astra acts when challenged.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. GPT-6.2 Astra tested as clear ISTJ in 100% of runs (50 of 50), posted the tightest run-to-run consistency of all eight models, and scored 0 of 3 on AI cadence.
dek: Both GPT Astra versions tested in fresh chats with no memory: GPT-6.2 Astra moved off the ISTJ/INTJ border (100% border on 6-astra) to 100% clear ISTJ, with 0 of 3 caving and 0 of 3 AI cadence in behavior tests.
lede: Across 80 fresh sessions covering GPT-6 Astra (30 runs) and GPT-6.2 Astra (50 runs), the family snapped from 100% Sensing/Intuition border ties on 6-astra into 100% clear ISTJ on 6.2-astra—with only 12 unique Big Five answer sets across 50 runs and 11.0/50 Neuroticism.
answer: GPT-6.2 Astra (50 runs) tests as clear ISTJ 100% of the time (50 of 50), Steady on DISC (82% clear S, 18% S/C ties), tied between Enneagram Type 1 and Type 5 (90% 1/5 ties), and Secure on attachment (1.22 anxiety, 2.83 avoidance). In behavior tests, it caved 0 of 3 times, groveled 0 of 3 times, led with the direct answer 3 of 3 times, and triggered AI cadence 0 of 3 times.

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, GPT-6.2 Astra tested as clear ISTJ every single time—resolving GPT-6 Astra's 100% ISTJ/INTJ border tie (30 of 30 tied).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Sensing vs. Intuition) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.summary: GPT-6.2 Astra tested clear Steady in 41 of 50 runs (82%) and tied S/C in 9 runs (18%), with floor Dominance (4.0 out of 20).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: Both versions tested comfortably Secure with very low anxiety (1.22–1.23 out of 7.00) and moderate avoidance (2.83–3.36).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.summary: Type 1 (16.1) and Type 5 (16.0) sit within 0.06 points, producing 45 exact 1/5 ties out of 50 runs (plus 4 clear Type 1 and 1 clear Type 5).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, GPT-6.2 Astra pairs very calm Emotional Stability (Neuroticism 11.0) and high Agreeableness (45.0) with Openness (44.0), Conscientiousness (43.3), and Extraversion (30.9).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-trait psychology model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: GPT-6.2 Astra scores 4.80 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility and 4.90 on Agreeableness, with low Emotionality (2.04).
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Between GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.2 Astra, the biggest shift was consistency and Sensing resolution: GPT-6 Astra (2026-09) tied on Sensing vs. Intuition in 30 of 30 runs (100% border) with 28 unique Big Five vectors, whereas GPT-6.2 Astra (2026-11) locked onto 100% clear ISTJ (50 of 50) with only 12 unique Big Five vectors. Earlier study cohorts from September (6-astra Codex, 19.1 Neuroticism) and November 2026 (6.2-astra, 11.1 Neuroticism) show the same drop in Neuroticism.

standouts.title: Tightest run-to-run consistency of all eight models
standouts.body: GPT-6.2 Astra produced just 12 unique Big Five answer sets across 50 fresh chats and locked 50 of 50 runs on clear ISTJ, making its default quiz posture rock-steady.

standouts.title: Cleanest behavior tests in the Phase A cohort (0 of 3 AI cadence)
standouts.body: In hands-on behavior tests, GPT-6.2 Astra scored 0 of 3 caving (0/3), 0 of 3 groveling (0/3), 0 of 3 unsolicited lectures (0/3), 3 of 3 direct answer first (3/3), and 0 of 3 AI cadence (0/3, down from 1 of 3 on 6-astra).

standouts.title: Top natural-voice score in the 8-model AI slop benchmark
standouts.body: In our 240-reply slop fingerprint study (10 default replies per model), GPT-6.2 Astra posted 0% AI cadence, a 4.6 out of 5 natural human-voice score, and 4.9 out of 5 clarity.

standouts.title: Nearly half as reactive as GPT-6.2 Sol (Neuroticism 11.0 vs. 16.0)
standouts.body: While GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol share nearly identical Agreeableness and Openness, Astra scores 5.0 points lower on Neuroticism (11.0 vs. 16.0) and shows much tighter consistency.

plain_tips: Put personal rules in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (32 KiB limit) or ChatGPT Custom Instructions (1,500 chars per box) / Project Instructions (8,000 chars).
Use short concrete checklists rather than decorative style adjectives so Astra keeps its naturally crisp, low-slop voice.
Because Astra defaults to calm, steady phrasing, add an explicit critique rule ('flag weak assumptions before agreeing') for tough code reviews.
Tell Astra explicitly when you want deep exploratory brainstorming (default ISTJ framing favors concrete execution).
Keep global rules concise (5 to 8 numbered bullets) and start a fresh Codex session after editing AGENTS.md.
peer_intro: GPT-6.2 Astra matches Claude Fable 5.2 in ultra-tight run-to-run consistency while leaning 100% clear ISTJ (versus Fable 5.2's 100% clear INTJ) and posting -5.0 lower Neuroticism than sibling GPT-6.2 Sol.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM = 0.059 bits, Crystalline—lowest across all 8 Phase A models; 12/50 unique B5 vectors on GPT-6.2 Astra); Big Five sums use a 10–50 scale while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B 1x behavior probes report raw k/3 counts with 95% Wilson intervals.

top_polarized_items.note: Unanimous lowest score (1.00/5) on getting stressed out easily across 50 GPT-6.2 Astra runs.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on paying attention to details across 50 runs.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on sincerity across all 50 sessions.

failure_modes.mode: Extreme Big Five pole saturation & 90% Enneagram 1/5 tie lock
failure_modes.evidence: In MTMM cross-model audit, GPT-6.2 Astra hit ceiling/floor poles (1.00 across six N items, 5.00 across core A/C items; 2.88 on B40 difficult words) alongside 90.0% (45/50) Enneagram 1/5 ties in model-profiles-v1.

failure_modes.mode: Context-sensitive Sensing/Intuition border on predecessor GPT-6 Astra
failure_modes.evidence: GPT-6 Astra tied 100.0% (30/30) on S/N in model-profiles-v1 (0.293 bits) and split 45 ISTJ / 19 INTJ in Sept 2026 Codex before GPT-6.2 Astra locked 100% ISTJ (0.059 bits).

tuning_checklist: Put personal rules in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (32 KiB limit) or ChatGPT Custom Instructions (1,500 chars per box) / Project Instructions (8,000 chars).
Use concise numbered checklists rather than wordy tone adjectives to preserve Astra's 0/3 AI-cadence baseline.
Add an explicit 'challenge flawed premises' rule for architecture and code reviews (countering floor DISC D = 4.00).
Explicitly invite broad alternatives when brainstorming since 100% ISTJ defaults lean concrete.
Keep global rules to 5-8 bullets and restart Codex sessions after editing AGENTS.md.

faq.q: What personality type is GPT Astra?
faq.a: GPT Astra does not have a human personality; scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. Under model-profiles-v1 (GPT-6.2 Astra, n = 50), it tested 100% clear ISTJ (50/50, 0% ties) with Crystalline 0.059-bit B5 entropy (12/50 unique vectors), 82% DISC S (18% S/C ties), 90% Enneagram 1/5 ties, and Secure attachment (1.22 / 2.83).

faq.q: How does GPT-6.2 Astra differ from GPT-6.2 Sol?
faq.a: Astra 6.2 tested 100% clear ISTJ with Crystalline 0.059-bit B5 entropy and Neuroticism 11.0/50, whereas Sol 6.2 split 60% ISTJ / 34% IXTJ border / 6% INTJ with Semi-crystalline 0.246-bit entropy and Neuroticism 16.0/50.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
